title: "Kernel Principal Component Analysis"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Overview

This example demonstrates Kernel PCA with an RBF kernel on a 6×3 data matrix
using the `aoclda` package.

```{r library}
library(aoclda)
```

## Define Data

```{r data}
A <- matrix(c(
    1.0,  2.0, -1.0,
    3.0, -1.0,  0.5,
    0.5,  1.5,  2.0,
   -2.0,  0.0,  1.0,
    1.5, -0.5, -1.5,
   -1.0,  1.0,  0.0
), nrow = 6, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

X <- matrix(c(
    0.5, -1.0,  1.5,
   -0.5,  2.0, -1.0,
    1.0,  0.0,  0.5
), nrow = 3, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
```

## Fit and Transform

```{r kpca}
kpca <- KernelPCA$new(n_components = 2L, kernel = "rbf", gamma = 0.5)
kpca$fit(A)
transformed <- kpca$transform(X)
```

## Results

```{r results}
cat("Eigenvalues:\n")
print(kpca$eigenvalues)

cat("\nScores (training data projected):\n")
print(kpca$scores)

cat("\nTransformed test data:\n")
print(transformed)

cat("\nResolved gamma:", kpca$gamma_, "\n")
```

## With Inverse Transform

```{r inverse}
kpca_inv <- KernelPCA$new(n_components = 2L, kernel = "rbf", gamma = 0.5,
                           fit_inverse_transform = TRUE)
kpca_inv$fit(A)
projected <- kpca_inv$transform(A)
reconstructed <- kpca_inv$inverse_transform(projected)

cat("Reconstructed data:\n")
print(reconstructed)
```
